blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements per Zscaler cloud for Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA). Zscaler will email a notification to your organization's registered support contacts approximately one week before your cloud is upgraded. To see scheduled maintenance updates for your cloud, visit the Trust Portal.

blocks.heading: Software Upgrade for Viewing Files in Isolation

To learn more, see Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.

DLP Intent Visibility Into Suspicious User Behavior
Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Intent provides visibility into potential insider risk by identifying user behaviors that might indicate suspicious activity, including:

blocks.heading: Support for Personal Email Detection in Outbound Email DLP Policy

blocks.text: The Zscaler service supports configuring your Outbound Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy rules to include detection of personal email addresses. When you select this option, the rule detects when end users attempt to send sensitive data to their personal email address by matching the user’s organizational name with recipient names on external email domains (e.g., Gmail or Yahoo). This option ensures that the rule is enforced only when the recipient is the sender’s personal email address.
See image.
A filter and column, Personal Email, is added to the Email DLP Insights Logs page to display the user’s personal email address when the email is sent to the user's personal email address.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Outbound Email Policy Rules, Email DLP Insights Logs: Filters, and Email DLP Insights Logs: Columns.

To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants, Authorizing a Custom Zscaler Connector for Slack, About SaaS Security Scan Configuration, and Configuring SaaS Security Scan Schedules.

blocks.heading: Support for New Match Type on Custom DLP Dictionaries

blocks.text: The Zscaler service supports the following predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) dictionaries:
The parent dictionaries contain predefined sub-dictionaries, and each sub-dictionary can be individually referenced in your DLP engines.

blocks.heading: Secure Email Gateway Support in Outbound Email DLP Policies

blocks.text: You can use Zscaler Outbound Email Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies with your secure email gateway (SEG) to prevent the exfiltration of sensitive data by enforcing policy rules on email content sent to external domains, including content in subject lines, body text, and attachments. As part of your larger DLP strategy, Zscaler Outbound Email DLP for SEGs lets you use the same DLP policy tools that you already use across other channels (i.e., Inline Web DLP, Endpoint DLP, and SaaS Security Data at Rest Scanning DLP), eliminating the need for different DLP point solutions and the operational overhead involved in maintaining those solutions. Additionally, you can monitor outbound email activity with dashboards, reports, and NSS feeds. This enhancement supplements existing Outbound Email DLP support for Microsoft Exchange and Gmail.
Because of recent enhancements to next-hop validation that enforce stricter security checks during SMTP connections, the Zscaler service:

blocks.item: Strictly enforces SSL/TLS for secure SMTP connections.
Performs server certificate validation that requires the presented certificate to be valid and trusted.
Does not allow self-signed, expired, or otherwise invalid certificates.

blocks.text: As you set up Email tenants in the Zscaler Admin Console (Policies > Data Protection > Policy > Email Tenants), you have the option to select an SEG tenant.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Email Tenants and Configuring SEGs for Zscaler Outbound Email DLP.

blocks.heading: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience for File Transfers

blocks.text: The following updates have been made to the end user isolation experience for Zero Trust Browser:

blocks.item: Download Completion: When a user downloads a file while in isolation, a temporary notification appears to confirm when the file has completed downloading. The user can click the View button from the notification to see the file name and location in the Protected Storage. Additionally, they can click the Protected Storage icon from the Zero Trust Mode menu to open the Protected Storage section and view all file transfer notifications.

Upload Options: A user can upload a file in multiple different ways while in isolation, such as using the Upload File button in the Protected Storage and uploading files from their local machine to a website.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience and Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.

blocks.heading: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience Session Indicator & Menu

blocks.text: The Zero Trust Mode icon that indicates a live isolation session for Zero Trust Browser hides an expandable menu for the user to access different functions:

blocks.item: The Protected Storage icon allows users to view all file transfers for the isolation session.
The Clipboard icon allows users to view notifications about clipboard functions and restrictions.
The Print icon allows users to view options and information for printing settings.
The Troubleshoot icon allows users to start a debug session, view network latency, access ip.zscaler.com, or export isolation session logs.
The Information icon allows users to view the settings configured by admins for an isolation profile. This includes user restrictions and disabled tools.

blocks.text: Clicking the checkmark Zero Trust Mode icon at the bottom of the menu collapses the options back under the floating icon.
See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience.

blocks.text: Instead of classifying all new applications as Unsanctioned, you can use new Application Status labels Unclassified and Under Review, to classify applications more appropriately. The label Unclassified means the applications haven't been evaluated for risks yet, and Under Review means they are undergoing due diligence.
See image.

Moreover, the SaaS Security Report for each cloud application now displays detailed information about security attributes including their certificate validity, WAF name, CVE ID, breach URL, and so on. More information appears in brackets next to the Yes and No signals.

Zscaler Endpoint Context extends the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) to provide unified cloud-to-endpoint visibility, detection, and dynamic risk-based policy enforcement. This functionality integrates real-time endpoint application data with industry-leading cloud intelligence to help your Security Operations Center (SOC) teams defend your organization from modern, sophisticated, AI-accelerated attacks that often bypass traditional siloed security tools.

Endpoint Context takes advantage of extensive data available from Zscaler Client Connector to provide an inventory of commonly abused applications that reside on each endpoint, both actively running and at rest, and enumerates a rich data set related to each application, including application name, publisher, total instances of an application, install path, etc.

Custom IPS is supported on Zscaler's public cloud, allowing you to create and deploy custom IPS signature rules without requiring any additional infrastructure (previously required a Private Service Edge deployment). You can inspect traffic transiting the Zscaler cloud against your custom signatures, irrespective of whether it is forwarded to a Public, Private, or Virtual Service Edge.
To enable Custom IPS with your Advanced Firewall subscription, contact your Zscaler Account team.
With this upgrade, the following enhancements are also made to Custom IPS:

blocks.item: Applicable to decrypted web traffic (decrypted via SSL Inspection) in addition to non-web traffic.
Extended support for HTTP protocol-aware signatures, so signature rules can include HTTP-specific options.

Signature rule validation occurs in two stages before deployment: static validation (currently supported) that checks rules for syntax errors, duplication, and based on other predefined conditions; dynamic validation (newly added) that runs signatures against designated packet captures to ensure efficient resource usage and optimal performance. The signature is enabled after both validations are completed. These transitions are indicated by new statuses.
View the newly added actions to initiate dynamic validation of signature rules.
In the Add Signature Rule (and Edit Signature Rule) window, a Save & Promote button is added to trigger dynamic validation of the rule.

The Enable Signature Rule toggle button is not accessible until the rule moves to the Enable Ready state with the successful completion of dynamic validation. There is no change to the existing Save option, which continues to save the rule after successful static validation.
On the Custom Signature Rules page, a Promote All button is added to initiate dynamic validation of all rules at once.
Logs showing custom signature matches for better visibility and easier troubleshooting.
Increased the custom signature rule limit to 1,000 (previously 500).

blocks.text: To learn more, see About Custom IPS Signature Rules, Configuring Custom IPS Signature Rules, and Specifications & Limitations for Custom IPS Signature Rules.

blocks.heading: Enhanced Flexibility in the URL Filtering Policy Rule Creation

blocks.text: You can apply either OR or AND logical operator between the Users, Groups, and Departments criteria in the URL Filtering Policy rules. This allows you to create granular policy rules using a combination of logical operators (i.e., OR or AND) between these criteria. As part of this update, up and down arrows are added to the logical operators between these criteria in the Add/Edit URL Filtering Rule window.
To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.

You can also add up to three Groups fields by clicking the Add icon next to the Groups field, and they are connected with a logical AND operator. This allows you to create rules that are triggered when they match the selected groups in all the Groups fields.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the URL Filtering Policy.

blocks.heading: Enhancement to Zscaler Cloud Performance Test Tool

blocks.text: The Zscaler Cloud Performance Test Tool allows you to view only the domain part of the traffic or email, and the user name is hidden. For example, johndoe@zscaler.com is visible as xxxxxxx@zscaler.com.

To learn more, see Using the Zscaler Cloud Performance Test Tool.

blocks.heading: Sandboxing Password-Protected PDF Files for Isolation

blocks.text: Zscaler Isolation now supports password-protected PDF files to be sandboxed for Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA). If ZIA Sandbox determines that the file is safe, users can download the original PDF. If ZIA Sandbox determines that the file is malicious, users cannot download the original PDF to their local device, and Zscaler stores the password for the duration of the isolated session. If the PDF can be rendered within the isolated browser, users can download the sanitized version of the PDF.

After the PDF is downloaded into the Isolation container, it opens on the user's device automatically, and they are prompted for the file password. Users are allowed unlimited incorrect password attempts.
To learn more, see About Sandbox Integration with Isolation and Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.
